newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank debentures not protected by DIC--banker.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank debentures not protected by DIC--banker.

text.p: Bank debentures issued by long-term credit banks are not covered by Japan"s deposit insurance act, the chairman of the Federation of Bankers Associations of Japan said on Tuesday.
The law was enacted to protect depositors against business difficulties at financial institutions.

Federation chairman Shunsaku Hashimoto told a regular news conference: "Bank debentures are not the target of insurance premiums paid (by financial institutions), and are not meant to be covered by the premiums." Corp (DIC) by financial institutions to provide a pool of funds to protect depositors. The DIC is a semi-governmental body set up to carry out the provisions of the deposit insurance act.

Hashimoto also said that he could not judge whether it was appropriate or not for Taku Yamasaki, a senior official of Japan"s ruling Liberal Democratic Party, to have said last week that creditors holding bank debentures may be protected through the use of various types of government funds.
"I did not directly hear how LDP policy chief Yamasaki made the remarks," Hashimoto said, declining to make further comment.
Hashimoto, also president of Sakura Bank Ltd, said he considers that recent remarks made by Japan"s Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka were aimed at stabilising Japan"s financial system.
Mitsuzuka said recently that his ministry would firmly support Japan"s major 20 banks in their efforts to resolve their bad loan problems.
"We must make utmost efforts to improve financial health on our own, but the minister"s comments were very supportive...," Hashimoto said.
